scoring_justification: Checker recomputes integrated benzene density near the metal wall and electric field at z=0.9 nm from the agent's raw CSV profiles, verifying the published desorption trend (Na/Na vs Cl/Cl) and unscreened field without trusting any self-reported metric.

hidden_assets.purpose: Thresholds for benzene density ratio and electric field magnitudes
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Inferred from paper's Figure 1 (benzene density profiles) and Figure 3 (electric field) and the narrative description of desorption in Na/Na system and unscreened field.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Thresholds chosen to match the qualitative behavior: integrated density ratio < 0.2 captures the drastic desorption; NaNa field > 3 V/nm reflects the unscreened field of ~7.9 V/nm near the metal, and ClCl field < 1 V/nm reflects the screened/local field near zero.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Thresholds are derived from published observable trends, not arbitrary; they are consistent with a correct reproduction as modelled in the reference solve.sh.

outputs.description: Number density profiles of benzene center-of-mass along the surface normal for Na/Na and Cl/Cl systems. The checker will recompute integrated densities from this table to verify the desorption trend.
Average electric field z-component profile for each system. The checker will recompute the field strength at specified positions to verify the unscreened field in the Na/Na system.

output_contract.notes: The scored artifacts are the raw profiles; no gold values or tolerances are disclosed. The hidden checker independently recomputes metrics from these profiles.

target.description: Integrated density of benzene near the metal wall (z ∈ [0.7, 0.931] nm) must be drastically lower for NaNa than for ClCl, reflecting desorption.
Electric field at z ≈ 0.9 nm must be >3 V/nm for NaNa and <1 V/nm for ClCl, confirming unscreened vs screened field.
